input: Research grants for small creative businesses

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Creative businesses span a huge range — visual arts, music, design, film, crafts, fashion, writing — and grants are often sector-specific, so knowing the exact creative field narrows the search dramatically.
Grant eligibility is almost always geography-dependent; a US federal grant, a UK Arts Council grant, or a city-level grant require entirely different research paths.
Many grants target specific founder demographics (women, minorities, veterans, youth) or business structures (sole trader vs. LLC vs. nonprofit), which filters which grants are even eligible.
The business's age, revenue size, and number of employees often determine eligibility thresholds; knowing these rules out grants that won't apply.
The user may want grants for a specific purpose — startup costs, equipment, hiring, marketing, or a project — and grants are usually tied to a declared use of funds.
Understanding how soon the user needs to apply (urgent deadline vs. ongoing research) determines whether to prioritise currently open grants or build a comprehensive long list.
The user might want a shortlist of the top 5 best-fit grants, a step-by-step application guide, or a broad landscape overview — the desired output shapes the entire plan.

gold.taskTitle: Research grants for small creative businesses
gold.taskDescription: Find suitable grant opportunities for a small creative business to apply for funding.

questions.title: What specific creative field is your business in?
questions.description: Identify the exact creative sector (e.g., visual arts, music production, graphic design, film, crafts, fashion) to target sector-specific grants.

questions.title: What country, state, or city is the business based in?
questions.description: Establish the geographic location to filter grants by eligibility jurisdiction — national, regional, or local.

questions.title: Who owns or leads the business — any specific demographics?
questions.description: Determine whether the owner identifies with groups that unlock targeted grants (e.g., women-owned, minority-owned, veteran-owned, under 30) and the legal business structure.

questions.title: How old is the business and what is its annual revenue?
questions.description: Capture business age and revenue figures to match eligibility criteria, since many grants cap turnover or require a minimum trading period.

questions.title: What would the grant funding specifically be used for?
questions.description: Clarify the intended use of funds — startup costs, equipment purchase, a creative project, hiring, marketing — as grants are typically tied to declared funding purposes.

questions.title: Do you have a deadline in mind for applying?
questions.description: Understand the urgency — whether the user needs currently open grants with near-term deadlines or wants a long-term pipeline of opportunities.

questions.title: What does a useful end result look like for you?
questions.description: Define the desired output — a ranked shortlist of grants, a full application guide, a broad landscape overview, or a calendar of deadlines — to shape the research plan accordingly.
